How to play

  1. Free every sun. A sun is freed when a full row or column through it clears. Any colours count.
  2. Bring the big windows back to light. In a picture chapter, each level you finish lights one part of a big stained-glass window with the suns you freed. Ten levels light the whole window; look at it from the map.
  3. Drag pieces onto the board. The Pieces count includes the three in the tray. Pieces don't rotate. Changed your mind? Let go anywhere off the board and the piece goes back to its spot. A level deals the same pieces on every try.
  4. Swipe a row or column to slide it one step. Glass that slides off one end comes back on the other. Each slide uses 1 shift. Changed your mind? Move your finger off the line before you let go and it slides back for free.
  5. Earn shifts back by clearing lines with one move: 2 lines at once earns 1 shift, 3 or more earns 2. You can hold 9 at most.
  6. Line up the gaps in neighbouring rows so one piece fills them all.
  7. Bolted panes pin their row and column. Prisms clear the line across them too.
  8. Ruby suns come free only when 2 or more lines clear at once. Vanes let their row or column slide only the way they point.
  9. The daily rose. Once your first window is whole, the chapel offers one more window each day. Solving it sets a pane in that month's rose; a day you miss can still be played until the month ends.
  10. Rewind takes back your last move, twice per try. Moves you take back don't count. A third rewind costs an ad. Before the ad, the game looks one move back, and plays the ad only if it finds a way to win from there.
  11. Par. Win a level in its par number of moves and that part of the window is leaded in gold. Gild all ten parts and the whole window is.

Start from the beginning?

You go back to level 1. Your gilding, the levels you've opened and the light in every window are wiped, and the intros show again. This can't be undone.
